name: theme-switcher
summary: Offers browser-local selection among app-defined theme choices without owning theme CSS.

agent.useWhen: An app offers a small browser-local choice among app-defined visual themes.
agent.avoidWhen: The preference is server-owned, affects query or account state, or requires navigation/network activity. Native readiness covers literal static-page declarations, not runtime bindings or live-region replacement.

invariants: Two to eight choices have unique safe token values, localized nonblank labels, and icons from the caller's locked closed geometry map.
Choice names are application-defined; the package does not restrict them to built-in themes and does not provide theme CSS.
defaultChoice, systemLightTheme, and systemDarkTheme must each match a configured choice; systemLightTheme and systemDarkTheme must name concrete choices, not system.
Optional targetId is a safe DOM ID, never a selector; omission explicitly targets documentElement. Only data-cui-theme is written.
Browser-local storage defaults to clanker-theme and may be disabled with storageKey null; denied storage falls back to in-memory selection.

System selection writes the configured concrete palette to data-cui-theme, while preserving system as the selected/stored preference; media changes and BFCache restoration re-resolve it. This keeps Native reference themes explicitly opted in rather than relying on ambient app CSS.

Each theme target must have only one selector owner. Replaced controls rebind without losing a valid local preference; removed owners and explicit cleanup release listeners without undoing or rewriting the app-owned target's current theme.
Controls are hidden before enhancement and meaningful fallback text remains visible without JavaScript; enhanced buttons expose aria-pressed.
No app/query/server preferences, routes, network requests, or app-defined CSS are owned. The fragment contains exactly one [[themeSwitcher]] slot.
